name: Question 17
problem:
Consider a function $m(t)$ such that its Laplace transform is $L{m(t)}=M(s)$ for $s>{s}_{0}.$ Suppose we wish to find $L{{e}^{-8t}m(t)}.$ Select the correct options in the reasoning below.By definition of the Laplace transform, we can write 

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{-8t}m(t)} & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{{field-1}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{{field-2}}\,m(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={{field-3}}\,\text{for}\,{{field-4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider a function m(t) such that its Laplace transform is L{m(t)}=M(s) for s>s0. Suppose we wish to find L{e−8tm(t)}. Select the correct options in the reasoning below.By definition of the Laplace transform, we can write

 
e−st⋅e8tm(t)
est⋅e8tm(t)
e−st⋅e−8tm(t)
est⋅e−8tm(t)
 
e−(s−8)t
e−(s+8)t
e(s−8)t
e(s+8)t
 
M(s+8)
M(s)
M(s−8)
 
s>s0+8
s>s0
s>s0−8
L{e−8tm(t)}=∫0∞{(e−st⋅e8tm(t))(S0)}dt=∫0∞{(e−(s−8)t)(S1)}m(t)dt={(M(s+8))(S2)}for{(s>s0+8)(S3)}.
